description: Reverse-ETL sink: mirror an upstream DataFrame into Stripe customers. Stripe has no native upsert endpoint and neither email nor any custom field is globally unique, so this supports two lookup strategies (match_by: email or metadata) depending on your data's guarantees.

inputs.description: pandas DataFrame from an upstream asset. Each row -> one Stripe customer (upserted via key_column, matched by email or metadata).

outputs.description: Dagster asset materialization with metadata. No downstream data -- write side effect lands in Stripe.

upstream_asset_key.label: Upstream Asset Key
upstream_asset_key.description: Asset providing the DataFrame. Mutually exclusive with source.

source.label: Source
source.description: Inline source config (sql/csv/inline). Mutually exclusive with upstream_asset_key.

key_column.label: Key Column
key_column.description: Upstream column holding a stable unique key. Written to each customer's metadata.dagster_key field; used to search for matches on subsequent runs.

extra_metadata_columns.label: Extra Metadata Columns
extra_metadata_columns.description: Additional columns whose values get written into the Stripe customer's metadata dict.

metadata_key_field.label: Metadata Key Field
metadata_key_field.description: Name of the metadata field used to store the dedup key.

match_by.label: Match By
match_by.description: How to match rows to existing customers: 'email' (immediately consistent) or 'metadata' (more precise but eventually consistent, up to 30s+ indexing lag).

batch_size.label: Batch Size
batch_size.description: Max upstream rows per run (safety cap).

name: Stripe Customer Upsert
